label: prf:mass-energy-equivalence
title: Proof of mass energy equivalence
html:
Proof. Proof of mass energy equivalence

Proof sketch. The proof proceeds via the Reshetikhin--Turaev invariant in a ribbon category, with the q-connection decomposition providing the conversion factor.

Step 1: Ribbon trace computes crossing energy. In the rigid monoidal category \mathbf{C}, the Frobenius--Hopf object A carries a ribbon structure (braiding + twist). For a composite \mathfrak{H} represented by the braid word \beta \in B_n, the Reshetikhin--Turaev construction [reshetikhin1991] gives

  \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{ribbon}}(\rho(\beta))
  = 
  \sum_{\text{crossings in } \beta}
  \begin{cases}
    q   & \text{positive crossing}, \\
    -q^{-1} & \text{negative crossing}.
  \end{cases}

The right-hand side is E_{\mathfrak{H}}. Each crossing weight is a spatial quantity: it measures the R-matrix coupling between horizontally adjacent fibres at strength q^{\pm 1}.

Step 2: Categorical mass measures vertical resistance. The categorical mass of a closed vortex \varrho \colon \mathbf{1} \to A is

  \mathfrak{m}_\varrho
  = 
  \bigl\lVert
    \mathrm{tr}\bigl(
      (\textstyle\int_A \otimes \mathrm{id})
      \circ \Delta \circ \varrho
    \bigr)
  \bigr\rVert

where \varrho denotes a generic closed vortex (morphism from the unit object). The Frobenius form \int_A and the comultiplication \Delta encode the q-connection. The mass measures resistance to transport through the comultiplication --- a vertical (Reeb) quantity, since \Delta encodes the q-connection whose temporal component has weight \hbar_q.

Step 3: The speed-of-light conversion. The q-connection A_q = q^{-1}A + \hbar_q\iota_\xi A\varTheta assigns weight q^{-1} to each spatial crossing and weight \hbar_q to each temporal tick. The ribbon trace sums spatial crossing weights (q^{\pm 1}), while the categorical mass sums temporal transport costs (\hbar_q per step through \Delta). Each crossing contributes q^{\pm 1} to energy and q^{\pm 1} \cdot \hbar_q / q^{-1} = q^{\pm 1} \cdot (q-1) to mass. The ratio is:

  \frac{E_{\mathfrak{H}}}{\mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{H}}}
  =  \frac{q^{-1}}{\hbar_q}
  \cdot \frac{q^{-1}}{\hbar_q}
  =  c_q^2
  =  \frac{1}{(q-1)^2}.
  \qquad\square
